featureIssue.title: [change] Suggest one compatible in-stock substitute when a SKU is unavailable
featureIssue.outcome: A counter assistant who requests a pack that is not on the shelf gets one concrete alternative in the same response, instead of a bare failure that sends them back to a separate lookup.
constraints: No internal classification field leaves the service.
At most one substitute is offered.
A substitute must be immediately reservable at the same site for the whole requested quantity.
A SKU whose status is not active is never suggested.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 An in-stock request is reserved and carries no suggestion.
AC-2 An out-of-stock request returns exactly one substitute.
AC-3 The substitute is the closest active in-stock member of the group.
AC-4 No internal classification field is ever serialised.
AC-5 A withdrawn SKU is never suggested.
AC-6 With no in-stock alternative the suggestion is null.
AC-7 The suggestion is stable across repeated identical requests.
AC-8 Held reservations reduce availability for later callers.
AC-9 Releasing a reservation restores availability.
AC-10 An inactive SKU is rejected rather than substituted.

specKit.what: GitHub spec-kit is an open-source toolkit for spec-driven development: it gives a repository a standard place and a standard shape for the specification, the plan, and the tasks that an agent works from.
specKit.howItRelates: This repository writes the same three artefacts by hand so the showcase stays dependency-light. spec-kit is the packaged version of the same discipline, and is the thing to reach for when more than one team needs the shape to be identical.
specKit.claimBoundary: Mentioned as an available toolkit. This repository does not run spec-kit, and does not claim to.

verifiableClaims: Every acceptance criterion in the specification maps to exactly one named test.
The mapping is checked in CI by scripts/verify.mjs --only acceptance, so a criterion without a test fails the build.
